answer: The terrace multiplier is published, charged in cipher, and cedar lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4015 identities would post 2903 proofs and burn roughly 5 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
